entries.source: Geschichte der Grafen von Wertheim von den ältesten bis zu ihrem Erlöschen im Mannsstamme im Jahre 1556, Nr. XXXIX. , S. 64, XXXIX.
entries.german:
Graf Rudolf von Wertheim verkauft dem Kloster Brom bach alle seine Güter in Reicholsheim und behält sich nur die Jurisdiction und die Lehensherrlich keit vor. 1285.

Nos Rudolfus Conus de Wertheim. Fidelis est literarum custodia, que rerum seriem eloquitur evidenter et emergen- tibus calumniis firma obviat veritate. Eapropter notum fore cupimus universis, ad quos presens scriptum pervenerit tam presentibus quam futuris, quod nos coadunata manu et grato assensu conjugis nostre Mechtildis vendidimus universa bona nostra in Reicholsheim culta et inculta, quesita et inquirenda, in bosco et in piano, in pascuis, pratis et silvis et molen- dinum in Teilbach viris religiosis Abbati et conventui in Brunnebach pro ducentis libris hall. que cum omni jure proprietatis, quomodo hactenus ea libere et quiete possedimus, eisdem tradidimus in proprietatem meram et liberam possi- denda, nullum jurisdictionem vel dominium in ipsis bonis vel nobis vel nostris posteris reservantes, exceptis hominibus utriusque sexus et judicio in platea duntaxat habendo, quod semper suberit nostre ditioni et juri, ita videlicet quod nul r„n\ r 43 latenus occasione ejusdem judicii hospitium vel expensas alt— quas circa ullos nostros homines faciendas ullo tempore re- quiramus in bonis prefatis, ne eis inferre gravamen vel damnum aliquod videamur in sue prejudicium libertatis, que ab omni angaria et exactione tam a nobis quam a nostris heredibus vel successoribus liberam esse decrevimus in per- petuum et securam sane notandum, quod omnes molitores ubicunque locorum fuerint residentes, qui in supradicto mo- lendino in Teilbach huc usque molere consueverunt, sicut inter nos et fratrem nostrum Bopponem Comitem in Wert- beim bone memorie quondam est ordinatum rationabiliter et diiTmitum, ibidem molere omni tempore, cum necesse ha- buerint, teneantur. Item memorie commemorandum, quod coloni predictorum bonorum, omnem censum, quem nobis ex ipsis bonis hactenus persolverunt, cujus summa con- sistit fere in viginti libris hall. cum pullis carnisp. fratri- bus monasteri i prelibati sine omni diminutione et protractione , singulis annis persolvent in terminis constitutis. Porro si colonorum aliquis predictorum casu vel necessitate qualibet contingente, residentiam vel debitam eulturam in bonis se- pi;dictis nequiverit habere, alium colonum pro se locabit, qui sit idoneus et sufficiens ad colendum et Odelis ac certus ad debitum censum reddendum, de predictorum fratrum tamen consilio et consensu. entries.english:
Count Rudolf von Wertheim sells all his properties at Reicholzheim to Brombach Monastery, reserving only jurisdiction and feudal lordship. 1285.

We, Rudolf, Count von Wertheim, wish it known to all, present and future, to whom this document comes, that reliable preservation of letters clearly sets out the course of events and firmly answers any accusations that may arise. Therefore, with the agreement and consent of our wife Mechtild, we have sold all our properties at Reicholzheim—cultivated and uncultivated, known and still to be discovered, in woodland and open country, in pastures, meadows, and forests—as well as the mill at Teilbach, to the religious men, the abbot and convent at Brombach, for two hundred pounds in Heller. We have transferred these properties to them to hold as free and absolute property, with all rights of ownership, in the same way that we have hitherto held them freely and peacefully. We reserve no jurisdiction or lordship over the properties for ourselves or our successors, except for the inhabitants, both male and female, and the right to hold court in the market square, which shall always remain subject to our authority and rights. In exercising that court, however, we shall never demand lodging or any expenses on account of it, or require our people to provide anything, so that we do not burden or harm the monks to the detriment of the liberty which we have decreed shall remain forever free and secure from every compulsory service and levy imposed by us, our heirs, or successors.

It should also be noted that all the millers, wherever they reside, who have hitherto been accustomed to grind at the aforesaid mill at Teilbach, shall continue to grind there whenever they need to, as was reasonably agreed and settled between us and our late brother Boppo, Count von Wertheim. The tenants of the aforesaid properties shall pay the brothers of the monastery every year, without reduction or delay and at the appointed times, all the rent they have hitherto paid us from those properties, amounting to about twenty pounds in Heller, together with the specified poultry. If any tenant, due to circumstance or necessity, cannot reside on or properly cultivate the properties, he shall appoint another tenant in his place who is fit and able to cultivate them and reliable in paying the rent, with the advice and consent of the aforesaid brothers. The tenants shall also faithfully pay the brothers, when due, the customary service called Haubrecht, through the year 1286. It should further be noted that a full and certain Warandia for these properties, beginning from the Feast of the Chair of Saint Peter in 1280, has been promised.

To secure this promise, we have provided the brothers with suitable guarantors: Eberhard Rufus and his brother Conrad, called the Younger; Eberhard, formerly vicedominus; the knights Friedrich, called Stahel, of Uissigheim; Kannapo, the schultheiss zu Wertheim; and Heinrich Schallbrunnen, Heinrich Bogeherre, and Heinrich Schrenken, citizens of Wertheim. They are both guarantors and witnesses to this agreement and promise, so that we may fulfill in deed what we have promised the brothers. To give this agreement due force and ensure that it remains inviolate, and to prevent any opportunity for accusation or evasion in the future, we have had this document written and sealed with our seal, the seal of our aforesaid wife Mechtild, and the seal of Lady Mechtild, widow of our late brother Boppo, Count von Wertheim. Done in the year of the Lord 1285.
